conflicts.description: Posting's status edit window: README.md and a 2026-10-01 decision transcript both state 30 minutes; minidon/config.py's edit_window_minutes default, its enforcement in statuses/service.py, and a test using a 61-minute offset all agree on 60 minutes.
conflicts.astInterpretation: Code/test view (DERIVED, 0.95): edit_window_minutes = 60 is the configured default, is the exact value compared against in edit_status, and the rejection test deliberately uses a 61-minute (not 31-minute) offset to trigger the 403 - three independent code artifacts agree on 60.
conflicts.llmInterpretation: Documentation view (STATED): README.md ## Posting states "Edit your own status within 30 minutes of posting"; a separate decision transcript dated 2026-10-01 independently records the same 30-minute figure and the business reasoning behind it.
conflicts.resolution: Unresolved by design (I-05). A human (BA / Product) must decide whether the code should change to 30 minutes, the documentation/decision record should change to 60, or a new decision is taken.

conflicts.description: minidon/lists/ (models.py, service.py) is confirmed dead/unreachable code by two independent structural passes, and the domain map deliberately excludes it from the capability hierarchy, but no human owner or product decision has been recorded for what happens to it.
conflicts.astInterpretation: ingestion-agent (warning MW-W01) and graph-agent (independent BFS from every entry point; orphans pkg:minidon.lists, minidon/lists/models.py, minidon/lists/service.py#create_list/#add_member) agree: no routes.py, not imported by minidon/main.py, not re-exported by minidon/models.py, zero test coverage. This structural fact is settled, not disputed.
conflicts.llmInterpretation: domain-map.md deliberately gives minidon/lists/ no L1-* id, lists it under Unmapped Code with owner "Unassigned - product decision needed (finish or remove Lists)", and raises (Boundary Question 5) whether, if completed, it would become a new L1 capability or an L2 sub-capability of Following.
conflicts.resolution: The "is this dead code" question is settled by code, independently, twice. What remains open is ownership: finish, remove, or leave dormant, and if finished, which capability boundary it joins. No winner picked; a human must assign a real owner.

conflicts.description: minidon/social/queries.py is owned by L1-following but consumed directly by Accounts, Posting, Timelines and Notifications; whether it should be a formally documented shared-kernel contract or remain an implicit import is undecided.
conflicts.astInterpretation: graph-agent: "the most reused cross-cutting module after accounts.service" - 8 in-degree, consumed by five of six capability clusters.
conflicts.llmInterpretation: ba-agent / domain-map.md: raises whether this implicit shared predicate layer should become a documented stable contract, since a change to visibility semantics here affects five modules at once.
conflicts.resolution: Not resolved here; a domain-modelling decision for a human.

conflicts.description: accounts/service.py#get_by_username is the graph's highest in-degree hotspot (18 incoming edges, called from 5 of 6 capability modules); whether it should be formalised as a stable identity-resolution API is undecided.
conflicts.astInterpretation: graph-agent hotspot analysis: inDegree 18, risk "high", "a behavior change here ripples across 5 of 6 wired capability modules."
conflicts.llmInterpretation: domain-map.md Boundary Question 2: should this be formalised as a stable identity-resolution API rather than a plain function import?
conflicts.resolution: Not resolved here; an API-design decision for a human.

conflicts.description: README.md documents "Posting" and "Interacting" as two separate feature sections; the code implements both in one package (minidon/statuses/), and the domain map merges them into one L1 capability with two L2 sub-capabilities.
conflicts.astInterpretation: No code-level boundary exists between "posting" and "interacting" behaviour - both live in minidon/statuses/service.py with no internal module split.
conflicts.llmInterpretation: README.md structures these as two ## headings (Posting, Interacting); domain-map.md (DERIVED) merges them into one L1-posting capability with two L2 sub-capabilities, and flags (Boundary Question 3) that this granularity choice needs business confirmation.
conflicts.resolution: Not resolved here; the merge is a reasonable DERIVED reading of the code, but whether it matches business intent is for a human to confirm.

conflicts.description: Moderation's "delete reported status" resolution calls Posting's soft_delete directly rather than through a narrower moderation-facing API, so it inherits Posting's cascading boost-deletion behaviour by implicit coupling.
conflicts.astInterpretation: minidon/moderation/service.py:71 calls minidon/statuses/service.py#soft_delete directly; statuses/service.py:142-150 shows the cascading boost-deletion this call inherits.
conflicts.llmInterpretation: ba-agent (moderation/rules-trace.md BR-015) and domain-map.md Boundary Question 4: Moderation reaches into Posting's write path; worth a boundary decision if Posting's delete semantics ever change independently.
conflicts.resolution: Not resolved here; an architecture decision for a human, independent of whether the current cascading behaviour is otherwise correct.

conflicts.description: README.md states a status can be boosted if you can see it; the code additionally restricts boosting to public/unlisted statuses only, so a followers-only status visible to a follower still cannot be boosted.
conflicts.astInterpretation: Code/test view (DERIVED, 0.85): BOOSTABLE = frozenset({Visibility.PUBLIC, Visibility.UNLISTED}); boosting a followers-only or direct status raises 403 even for a viewer who can see it, confirmed by test_followers_only_statuses_cannot_be_boosted.
conflicts.llmInterpretation: Documentation view (STATED): README.md ## Interacting states "Boost any status you can see to share it with your followers," with no visibility carve-out.
conflicts.resolution: Unresolved. Raised as an open question rather than a formal conflict in posting/rules-trace.md's own Conflict Log; the curator elevates it here per I-28 since README's claim is a falsifiable universal statement the code contradicts for two of four visibility levels.
